mainTopic: Whether גרים count as קהל, whom a גר may marry, and why a שתוקי and an אסופי are restricted only מדרבנן
overview: The גמרא finishes the מחלוקת between רבי יוסי, who lets a גר marry a ממזרת, and רבי יהודה, who forbids it. רבי יוסי uses all five times the תורה writes קהל for other purposes, so a קהל of גרים is not called קהל. The גמרא gives three ways רבי יהודה includes גרים: combining כהנים and לוים, combining the two שתוקי rules into one פסוק, or learning from 'הקהל חקה אחת לכם ולגר'. רבי יוסי answers that 'חקה אחת' breaks up that פסוק. Then come stories of רבי זירא and רבא teaching in מחוזא. The הלכה is that a גר may marry a כהנת (since women of good lineage were not warned against פסולים) and also a ממזרת, following רבי יוסי. Next, רבא teaches that by Torah law a שתוקי and an אסופי are fit, because the תורה bans only a definite ממזר. The fear that one of them might marry his sister is shown to be too rare to explain the rabbinic ban. The real reason is a מעלה the רבנן made for families of clean lineage. The amud ends as רבא בר רב הונא begins a ruling about a foundling found circumcised, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's five uses of the word קהל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes listing how רבי יוסי uses all five appearances of קהל, which leaves none for גרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: One קהל is for כהנים, one for לוים, and one for ישראלים. One permits a ממזר to marry a שתוקי, and one permits a שתוקי to marry a regular ישראל. A congregation of גרים is not called a קהל at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing its answer to why רבי יוסי allows a גר to marry a ממזרת. Every קהל in the פסוקים already has a job, so there is no קהל left over for גרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each קהל teaches who a ממזר may not marry (כהנים, לוים, ישראלים) or whom he may marry (a שתוקי). Since all five are used up, גרים are not included in 'קהל ה׳'. So a ממזר is allowed to marry a גיורת, and a גר is allowed to marry a ממזרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Congregation; the group a ממזר is forbidden to marry into
A child born from a forbidden relationship, who may not marry into the קהל
A person whose father is unknown, so it is a doubt whether he is a ממזר

phrases.english: One is for priests,
and one is for Levites,
and one is for Israelites,
and one is to permit a mamzer to a shetuki,
and one is to permit a shetuki to an Israelite.
A congregation of converts is not called a congregation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of רבי יוסי's reasoning that was begun before this section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: All five appearances of קהל are used for other purposes, so גרים are not included in קהל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the count that the rest of the sugya works with. רבי יהודה needs to find one 'extra' קהל in order to include גרים.

steps.title: How does רבי יהודה deal with the five uses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה can include גרים if all five appearances of קהל are already used.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה, how does he explain it?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. The גמרא is preparing to explain how רבי יהודה finds an extra קהל to include גרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה forbids a גר to marry a ממזרת, so he must hold that גרים are part of קהל. But רבי יוסי's list seemed to use up every קהל. The גמרא wants to know where רבי יהודה's source comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: A short question: 'And how does רבי יהודה handle this?'
The תנא who forbids a גר to marry a ממזרת

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: He's asking: if all five are used up, how does רבי יהודה include converts?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי יוסי's count to ask about the other side of the מחלוקת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which קהל רבי יהודה uses as his source for including גרים.

steps.title: כהנים and לוים come from one קהל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns כהנים and לוים from a single קהל, which frees one קהל for גרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: כהנים and לוים both come from one קהל. That leaves him an extra קהל to include the congregation of גרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. רבי יהודה combines כהנים and לוים into one קהל, so one קהל is left over for גרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי counted כהנים and לוים as two separate groups. רבי יהודה counts them as one group, which saves one קהל. He uses that extra קהל to include גרים, so a ממזר may not marry into them.

keyTerms.meaning: They come out (they are learned from)
It is left over for him

phrases.english: Priests and Levites are derived from one "congregation,"
so one remains for him for the congregation of converts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Combining כהנים and לוים frees one קהל, which רבי יהודה uses for גרים.

steps.title: Second answer: both שתוקי rules come from one קהל
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, רבי יהודה agrees that כהנים and לוים are two, but he learns both שתוקי rules from one פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: it is true that כהנים and לוים are two separate קהלים. But the rule allowing a ממזר to marry a שתוקי and the rule allowing a שתוקי to marry a ישראל both come from one קהל, the פסוק 'לא יבא ממזר בקהל ה׳'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to explain how רבי יהודה gets an extra קהל. This time he saves the extra קהל from the two שתוקי rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this answer רבי יהודה agrees with רבי יוסי that כהנים and לוים need separate sources. Instead, he takes the two leniencies about a שתוקי, which רבי יוסי learned from two separate קהלים, and learns them both from one פסוק. The next step shows how one פסוק teaches both.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer)
So too; it is indeed so
Shall not enter (shall not marry into)

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
indeed, they are two congregations,
phrases.notes: "They" means the כהנים and the לוים. Here רבי יהודה agrees with רבי יוסי that they are two.

phrases.english: but a mamzer with a shetuki and a shetuki with an Israelite
are derived from one "congregation" —
"A mamzer shall not enter the congregation of the Lord" —
phrases.notes: דברים 23:3

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָכִי נָמֵי, תְּרֵי קְהָלֵי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the question in step 2, instead of the answer in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two שתוקי leniencies come from one פסוק, which frees one קהל for גרים.

steps.title: How one פסוק teaches both שתוקי rules
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is read two ways: a definite ממזר is forbidden, and the definite קהל is forbidden to him. So a doubtful ממזר may marry in, and a ממזר may marry someone who is doubtful.
steps.simpleTranslation: Only a definite ממזר may not enter, so a doubtful ממזר may enter. And he may not enter only a definite קהל, so he may enter a doubtful קהל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows exactly how the single פסוק 'לא יבא ממזר בקהל ה׳' produces both leniencies about a שתוקי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ממזר' means a certain ממזר. That teaches that a שתוקי, who is only a doubtful ממזר, may marry a ישראל. The word 'קהל' means a certain, kosher קהל. That teaches that a ממזר may marry a שתוקי, who is not certainly part of the קהל.
steps.whatToRemember: In this answer, one פסוק gives two leniencies: a doubtful ממזר may marry a ישראל, and a ממזר may marry a doubtful person. This leaves a spare קהל for גרים.

phrases.english: It is a definite mamzer who may not enter,
but a doubtful mamzer may enter;
phrases.notes: A doubtful ממזר is the שתוקי. So he may marry a regular ישראל.

phrases.english: it is into a definite congregation that he may not enter,
but into a doubtful congregation he may enter.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַמְזֵר וַדַּאי הוּא דְּלֹא יָבֹא, הָא מַמְזֵר סָפֵק – יָבֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק quoted in step 4 teaches both rules.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ממזר is read as certain and the קהל is read as certain, which gives both leniencies from one פסוק.

steps.title: Third answer: רבי יהודה learns it from a different פסוק
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, all five קהלים are used just as רבי יוסי says, and רבי יהודה includes גרים from the פסוק 'הקהל חקה אחת לכם ולגר הגר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: these too (the definite and the doubtful) are two separate קהלים. רבי יהודה's reason comes from here: 'הקהל, there shall be one law for you and for the גר who lives among you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer. רבי יהודה does not need a spare קהל at all, because he learns about גרים from a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי יהודה agrees that the two שתוקי rules need two separate קהלים, so all five are used up. Instead, he reads 'הקהל ... ולגר' as one unit. That teaches that a גר is counted as part of the קהל, so a ממזר may not marry a גיורת.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
these too are two congregations,
phrases.notes: "These" means the definite ממזר rule and the doubtful one, and each needs its own קהל.

phrases.english: and the reason of Rabbi Yehuda is from here:
"The congregation, one statute
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:15

phrases.english: for you and for the stranger who sojourns."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָנֵי נָמֵי תְּרֵי קְהָלֵי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the idea of combining the שתוקי rules from step 4 and gives a completely different source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה learns from 'הקהל חקה אחת לכם ולגר' that a גר is part of the קהל.

steps.title: How does רבי יוסי read that פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוסי deals with the פסוק that seems to put גרים inside the קהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יוסי, what about this פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. The גמרא is preparing to explain why the פסוק does not prove anything for רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to say directly that גרים are part of the קהל. That would contradict רבי יוסי, who says a קהל of גרים is not called קהל. So the גמרא needs to explain how he reads it.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to רבי יוסי, how does he explain it?

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yosei?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the other side handles the פסוק brought for רבי יהודה in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי יוסי reads 'הקהל חקה אחת לכם ולגר'.

steps.title: 'חקה אחת' breaks up the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יוסי, the words 'חקה אחת' separate 'הקהל' from 'ולגר', so the פסוק does not put גרים in the קהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words 'חקה אחת' interrupt the topic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יוסי's reading. The words 'חקה אחת' break the פסוק into separate parts, so 'הקהל' is not linked to the גר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads 'הקהל ... לכם ולגר' as one phrase that puts the גר in the קהל. רבי יוסי says the words 'חקה אחת' come in between and cut the connection. So the גר is equal to ישראל in the law being discussed there, but he is not called 'קהל'.

keyTerms.meaning: It interrupted the matter; it breaks the connection between the parts of the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה has three possible sources for including גרים in the קהל. רבי יוסי rejects the פסוק source because 'חקה אחת' separates the word הקהל from the גר.

phrases.english: "One statute" interrupts the matter.
phrases.notes: Those words stand between 'הקהל' and 'ולגר', so the two aren't read together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'חקה אחת' separate 'הקהל' from 'ולגר', so the פסוק does not include גרים in the קהל.

steps.title: The ברייתא supports רב: women of good lineage may marry פסולים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says a גר, a freed slave and a חלל may all marry a כהנת. This supports רב's rule that women of good lineage were never forbidden to marry men who are פסולים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A convert, a freed slave and a חלל are all allowed to marry a כהן's daughter. This supports רב, since רב יהודה said in רב's name: women of good lineage were not warned against marrying disqualified men.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא it has been discussing backs up a known rule of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah's marriage restrictions of כהונה are placed on male כהנים, who may not marry certain women. They are not placed on the daughters of כהנים. So a כהנת may marry men who are פסולים לכהונה. Since the ברייתא lets her marry a גר, a freed slave and even a חלל, it fits רב's rule exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: A man born from a forbidden כהונה marriage, disqualified from כהונה
Women of good lineage were not warned against marrying disqualified men

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule of רב becomes the reason for the final הלכה in step 15 that a גר may marry a כהנת.

phrases.english: Both a convert and a freed slave
and a חלל are permitted to a כהן's daughter.
This supports רב,
as רב יהודה said in the name of רב:
Women of proper lineage were not warned
against marrying disqualified men.
phrases.notes: The ban is on the male כהן marrying certain women, not on a כהנת marrying certain men.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the רבי יוסי reading of the פסוק to a related ruling in the same ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that women of good lineage may marry פסולים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא permitting a גר, a freed slave and a חלל to marry a כהנת

steps.title: רבי זירא teaches in מחוזא that a גר may marry a ממזרת
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא publicly taught that a גר may marry a ממזרת, and the crowd pelted him with their אתרוגים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא taught in מחוזא: a convert is allowed to marry a ממזרת. Everyone threw their אתרוגים at him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. רבי זירא taught רבי יוסי's ruling in public, and the people reacted angrily.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling follows רבי יוסי: גרים are not counted as a קהל, so the ban on a ממזר entering the קהל does not stop a גר from marrying a ממזרת. The many converts in מחוזא heard this as saying they are not truly part of the Jewish people, and they were insulted.

keyTerms.meaning: A town in בבל with many converts

phrases.english: רבי זירא taught publicly in מחוזא:
A convert is permitted to a ממזרת.
Everyone pelted him
with their אתרוגים.
phrases.notes: The converts took it to mean they are not part of the real קהל, so they felt insulted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי יוסי's view from step 8 in a public setting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גר may marry a ממזרת

steps.title: רבא criticizes teaching this where many converts live
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks how anyone could teach such a ruling in a place full of converts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is there anyone who teaches something like this in a place where converts are common?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא comments on the story. He does not argue with the ruling itself, only with teaching it there in that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is rhetorical. It means 'one should not do this.' The problem is how and where the ruling was presented, since it was bound to hurt the converts' feelings. רבא's own teaching comes next as a better way to present it.

phrases.english: רבא said:

phrases.aramaic: מִי אִיכָּא דְּדָרֵישׁ מִילְּתָא כִּי הַאי
phrases.english: Is there anyone who teaches a matter like this
in a place where converts are common?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אִיכָּא דְּדָרֵישׁ מִילְּתָא כִּי הַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Criticizes the way רבי זירא presented his teaching in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Be careful how a sensitive ruling is taught in front of the people it affects.

steps.title: רבא teaches that a גר may marry a כהנת
steps.stepSummary: רבא taught in מחוזא that a גר may marry a כהנת, and the people honored him by carrying him on silks.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught in מחוזא: a convert is allowed to marry a כהן's daughter. They carried him on silks.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a public teaching that honors converts, and the people celebrate him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling is based on רב's rule from step 9: women of good lineage may marry פסולים. Even a כהנת may marry a גר. The converts saw this as raising their standing, so they honored רבא.

phrases.english: רבא taught publicly in מחוזא:
A convert is permitted to a כהן's daughter.
They carried him on silks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא's own better way of teaching, after his criticism in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גר may marry a כהנת

steps.title: רבא adds the ממזרת ruling and the people complain
steps.stepSummary: רבא then also taught that a גר may marry a ממזרת. The people told him he had spoiled his first teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then taught them again: a convert is allowed to marry a ממזרת. They said to him: you have ruined the first one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא repeats רבי זירא's ruling, and the crowd objects that he has undone the honor he gave them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people feel the two teachings pull in opposite directions. The first seemed to raise the converts' status, and the second seemed to lower it again. Their complaint sets up רבא's answer in the next step.

phrases.english: He then taught them again:
A convert is permitted to a ממזרת.
They said to him:
You have ruined the first one.
phrases.notes: They mean the honor from his first teaching is now lost.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the ruling from step 10, which seems to cancel the honor of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's adding of the ממזרת ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Allowing a ממזרת seems to lower the converts' status and undo the honor of the כהנת ruling.

steps.title: רבא explains that both rules help the גר
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that he did them a favor. A גר may now marry either a woman of high lineage or a ממזרת, as he wishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I did what is good for you. If he wants, he can marry from here, and if he wants, he can marry from here.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא shows that the second ruling does not take anything away. It gives the גר more people he is allowed to marry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The complaint saw the ממזרת ruling as an insult. רבא turns it around: it is an extra permission. A גר has the widest possible choice, from a כהנת all the way to a ממזרת.

phrases.english: He said to them:
What is good for you, I have done for you:
if he wants, he marries from here,
and if he wants, he marries from here.
phrases.notes: The first 'here' is women of good lineage, like a כהנת. The second is a ממזרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the people's complaint in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: the second ruling is an added permission, not an insult
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Allowing a ממזרת lowers the גר's status.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both rulings widen the גר's choices, so both help him.

steps.title: The הלכה: a גר may marry both a כהנת and a ממזרת
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows both rulings. The כהנת rule comes from רב's principle, and the ממזרת rule follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is: a convert may marry a כהן's daughter and may marry a ממזרת. He may marry a כהן's daughter because women of good lineage were not warned against marrying disqualified men. He may marry a ממזרת following רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling and names the source for each half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each half has its own basis. The כהנת half rests on רב's principle from step 9. The ממזרת half rests on רבי יוסי's view that גרים are not counted as a קהל, so the ממזר ban does not apply to them.
steps.whatToRemember: A גר may marry a כהנת, since women of good lineage were never forbidden to marry פסולים. He may also marry a ממזרת, following רבי יוסי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה about whom a גר may marry.

phrases.english: And the הלכה is:
a convert is permitted to a כהן's daughter
and permitted to a ממזרת.
Permitted to a כהן's daughter:
women of good lineage were not warned against marrying disqualified men;
and permitted to a ממזרת:
following רבי יוסי.
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי holds that גרים are not counted as a קהל, as in step 1.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the story into a final ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A גר may marry a כהנת (רב's principle) and a ממזרת (רבי יוסי).

steps.title: The משנה defines a שתוקי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a שתוקי is someone who knows his mother but not his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are they: a שתוקי is anyone who recognizes his mother, but not his father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה's next term. This sets up רבא's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שתוקי's mother is known, but his father is not. So we cannot be sure whether he is a ממזר. That doubt is what the next step deals with.

phrases.english: These are they: a שתוקי:
anyone who recognizes
phrases.notes: The משנה means he knows who his mother is, but not his father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The גמרא goes back to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שתוקי knows his mother but not his father.

steps.title: רבא: by Torah law a שתוקי is כשר, because most men are fit
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that by Torah law a שתוקי may enter the קהל. The reason is that most men are fit with the mother, and only a few would make her child a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: by Torah law a שתוקי is fit. What is the reason? Most men are fit with regard to her, and only a minority are unfit with regard to her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the Torah-level status of a שתוקי, and then the גמרא asks for his reason and answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father is unknown, so the Torah follows the majority. Most men are not related to the mother in a way that would make the child a ממזר, so the child is treated as כשר. This is only the Torah-level law, which is why רבא says 'דבר תורה.'

keyTerms.meaning: Fit, permitted to marry into the קהל

steps.confusionAlert: רבא only says a שתוקי is כשר 'by Torah law.' Do not assume this means he may marry anyone in practice.

phrases.english: רבא said:
By Torah law, a שתוקי is fit.
What is the reason?
Most are fit with regard to her,
phrases.notes: Most men are not related to her in a way that would make her child a ממזר.

phrases.english: and a minority are unfit with regard to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the Torah-level status of the שתוקי defined in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By Torah law a שתוקי is כשר, following the majority of men, who are fit with his mother.

steps.title: If the men came to her, we follow the majority
steps.stepSummary: רבא continues: if the father came to the mother, he separated from the majority, who are fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they went to her, anything that separates is considered to separate from the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues his reasoning from the last step. He shows that when the man came to the woman, we may follow the majority of men, who are fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that when something leaves its group, we treat it as coming from the majority of that group. If the father left the general population to come to her, we assume he came from the fit majority, so the child is not a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Anything that separates is treated as coming from the majority

phrases.english: And if they went to her,
phrases.notes: "They" means the men, one of whom fathered the child.

phrases.english: anything that separates, separates from the majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's reasoning that most men are fit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the man came to the woman, we follow the majority, and the child is presumed fit.

steps.title: But maybe she went to them, making it a fixed case
steps.stepSummary: רבא raises a problem: if she went to the men, the case is קבוע, and a קבוע case counts as half and half.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would you say? Perhaps she went to them. Then it is fixed, and anything fixed is considered like half and half.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises an objection to his own argument. If the woman went to where the men were, the majority rule does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the doubt happens at the item's fixed place, we do not follow the majority. We treat it as a 50-50 doubt instead. That would leave the שתוקי as a real ספק ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixed in its place; a doubt that happens where the item is located
It is treated like half and half, a full doubt

steps.confusionAlert: קבוע does not mean the majority changed. The majority is still fit, but in a fixed case the הלכה does not let us rely on it.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אָמְרַתְּ – דִּילְמָא אָזְלָה אִיהִי לְגַבַּיְיהוּ
phrases.english: What would you say, that perhaps she went to them?
Then it is fixed,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל קָבוּעַ כְּמֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: and anything fixed is considered like half and half.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אָמְרַתְּ דִּילְמָא אָזְלָה אִיהִי לְגַבַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the majority argument of step 18 by raising the case of קבוע.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of רוב to permit the שתוקי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If she went to the men, the case is קבוע, which counts as a 50-50 doubt, so רוב cannot be used.

steps.title: The Torah forbids only a definite ממזר
steps.stepSummary: Even if the case is a full doubt, the Torah's words show that only a definite ממזר is forbidden. A doubtful one may enter.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the Torah said, 'A ממזר shall not enter.' It is a definite ממזר who may not enter, but a doubtful ממזר may enter. Into a definite קהל he may not enter, but into a doubtful קהל he may enter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own objection. Even if the case is a 50-50 doubt, a ספק ממזר is still permitted by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ממזר in the פסוק is read as meaning a definite ממזר only. Likewise, the word קהל means a definitely fit congregation. So the question of קבוע no longer matters for Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: The congregation, meaning Jews of fit lineage

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule that a ספק ממזר is permitted מן התורה. Any ban on him is only מדרבנן.

phrases.english: But the Torah said: "A ממזר shall not enter"
phrases.notes: דברים 23:3

phrases.english: it is a definite ממזר who may not enter,
but a doubtful ממזר may enter.
Into a definite congregation he may not enter,
but into a doubtful congregation he may enter!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19: even a full doubt is permitted מן התורה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading of the פסוק that makes the objection irrelevant
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A קבוע case is a real doubt, so the שתוקי would be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah forbids only a definite ממזר, so even a ספק ממזר may enter the קהל.

steps.title: Then why did the רבנן forbid a שתוקי?
steps.stepSummary: If a שתוקי is fit by Torah law, why did the רבנן call him פסול?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for what reason did they say that a שתוקי is unfit?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that a שתוקי is permitted by Torah law, the גמרא asks why the משנה still calls him פסול. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the Torah allows him, the ban must be a rabbinic one. The question asks what concern lies behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: Unfit to marry a Jew of fit lineage
And for what reason did they say

phrases.english: And for what reason did they say a שתוקי is unfit?
phrases.notes: "They" are the חכמים of the משנה quoted in step 16.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 20: if he is permitted מן התורה, why is he forbidden?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the rabbinic ban on a שתוקי

steps.title: A גזירה so he won't marry his paternal sister
steps.stepSummary: The ban is a rabbinic decree, made out of fear that he might marry his sister from his unknown father.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree, lest he marry his sister from his father.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer: the רבנן made a גזירה because he does not know who his father is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is not that he is a ממזר. Since his father is unknown, he could marry a daughter of that same father without knowing she is his sister.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to prevent a problem

phrases.english: It is a decree, lest he marry his sister from his father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban is a גזירה, made out of fear that he might marry his paternal sister.

steps.title: Then a שתוקי should not marry a שתוקית either
steps.stepSummary: If that is the fear, a שתוקי should be forbidden to marry a female שתוקית, since she could be his paternal sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, a שתוקי should not marry a שתוקית, lest he marry his sister from his father!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason just given. A שתוקי is normally allowed to marry a שתוקית, yet the same fear should apply to her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A female שתוקית also has an unknown father. That father could be his own father. So the sister worry should forbid this match too.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, now that you say this
A female שתוקי, a woman whose father is unknown

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, שְׁתוּקִי – שְׁתוּקִית לֹא יִשָּׂא,
phrases.english: But if so, a שתוקי should not marry a שתוקית,
lest he marry his sister from his father!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה שְׁתוּקִי שְׁתוּקִית לֹא יִשָּׂא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The sister-decree reason for banning a שתוקי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same fear applies even more when both partners have unknown fathers, yet the marriage is allowed.

steps.title: Is there really that much immorality?
steps.stepSummary: It is far-fetched to think that all the unknown-father children in town come from the same man.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do all of these people go on acting immorally?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we do not assume one man fathered both of these children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Worrying about a שתוקי marrying a שתוקית would mean picturing one father behind many such births. That is not realistic, so no גזירה is needed.

phrases.english: Do all such people go on acting immorally to that extent?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two שתוקים might easily share the same father.
steps.terutzMaskana: We do not assume that much immorality, so a שתוקי may marry a שתוקית.

steps.title: By that logic, ban marrying a שתוקית's daughter too
steps.stepSummary: If we worried so much, a שתוקי could not marry even the daughter of a שתוקית, since her husband might be his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he should not marry the daughter of a שתוקית, lest he marry his sister from his father!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presses further to show the worry has no limit. Even the daughter of a שתוקית, born in a proper marriage, could be his sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man who married the שתוקית could be the same man who fathered the שתוקי. No one forbids this match. So the worry must be rejected for a different reason than how much immorality there is.

keyTerms.meaning: The daughter of a female שתוקי, born from a proper marriage

phrases.english: Then he should not marry the daughter of a שתוקית,
phrases.notes: Her father is known; the fear is that this same man also fathered the שתוקי.

phrases.english: lest he marry his sister from his father!

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּת שְׁתוּקִית לֹא יִשָּׂא שֶׁמָּא יִשָּׂא אֲחוֹתוֹ מֵאָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on step 24's answer by pointing to a case where immorality is not the issue.
steps.kashyaTarget: The sister-decree reason for banning a שתוקי (step 22)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The daughter of a שתוקית might share his father, yet no one forbids that match. So worrying about a sister mix-up cannot be what drives the ban.

steps.title: The sister fear is too rare to be the reason
steps.stepSummary: The daughter of a שתוקית is permitted because a sister mix-up is rare. In the same way, the general fear that a שתוקי will marry his sister is rare, so it cannot be why the רבנן made him פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is uncommon; so too here, it is uncommon!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that a sister mix-up is uncommon, so the decree 'lest he marry his sister' cannot explain why a שתוקי is פסול. This sets up the real reason in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees he may marry the daughter of a שתוקית, because a sister mix-up there is rare. By the same logic, the fear of marrying his sister is rare in general, and the רבנן do not make a גזירה for an uncommon case. So the reason given in step 22 falls away.
steps.whatToRemember: A שתוקי is fit מן התורה, since only a definite ממזר is forbidden. A sister mix-up is too uncommon for the רבנן to make a גזירה about it. So the 'lest he marry his sister' reason cannot explain the ban on his marrying a woman of fit lineage. The next step gives the real reason.

phrases.english: Rather, it is uncommon,
so too here it is uncommon!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָא שְׁכִיחָא הָכִי נָמֵי לָא שְׁכִיחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the permitted case of step 25 to show that the decree reason of step 22 does not hold.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A sister mix-up is uncommon, so the decree 'lest he marry his sister' cannot be the reason a שתוקי is פסול.

steps.title: The ban is a higher standard for lineage
steps.stepSummary: The real reason a שתוקי may not marry someone of clear lineage is that the Rabbis set a higher standard for lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the Sages made a higher standard regarding lineage.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the fear of marrying a sister was rejected, the גמרא gives the true reason for the ban. The Rabbis simply set a higher standard for family lineage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 showed that the sister fear is too rare to explain anything. So the ban on marrying people of clear lineage is not about a real fear of sin. It is an extra level of care, a מעלה, to protect clean family lines.

keyTerms.meaning: A higher standard; an extra level of strictness
They (the Sages) made or set up

steps.whatToRemember: A שתוקי may marry a שתוקית. He is kept only from people of clear lineage, because of a rabbinic מעלה ביוחסין.

phrases.english: Rather, they made a higher standard regarding lineage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected sister-fear reason with the true reason for the ban.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The שתוקי ban is a rabbinic higher standard for lineage, not a fear of marrying a relative.

steps.title: רבא: by Torah law a foundling is fit
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that by Torah law an אסופי is fit. A married woman would credit the child to her husband, so only a small group of mothers of a ממזר would abandon a baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: by Torah law a foundling is fit. Why? A married woman who has a child from another man claims her husband is the father, so she has no reason to abandon the baby. Who is left? Only a minority: betrothed women, and women whose husbands went overseas.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבא about the אסופי, a baby found abandoned. He says that by Torah law the baby is fit, and he starts to explain why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most babies who are ממזרים are born to married women. Those women just say the husband is the father and keep the baby. Only a few cases, an ארוסה or a woman whose husband is away, would have a reason to abandon a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: A foundling: a baby found abandoned, whose father and mother are both unknown
By Torah law (as opposed to rabbinic law)
Hangs it on; credits the child to
Betrothed women who are not yet living with their husbands

phrases.english: And רבא said:
By Torah law, a foundling is fit.
What is the reason?
A married woman credits the child to her husband.
What is left?
A minority of betrothed women,
and a minority whose husbands went overseas.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא, דְּבַר תּוֹרָה: אֲסוּפִי – כָּשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the שתוקי to a parallel teaching about the אסופי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By Torah law an אסופי is fit to marry into the community.

steps.title: The doubt is only half and half
steps.stepSummary: Many fit babies are also abandoned, by unmarried mothers or because of hunger. So the chance that a foundling is a ממזר is only half and half.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since there are also unmarried women who abandon babies, and also babies abandoned because of hunger, it comes out half and half.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues his reasoning. He weighs the few mothers of a ממזר who abandon babies against the many reasons fit babies get abandoned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unmarried woman's child is not a ממזר, and a family in hunger may abandon a fit child. Put together, these cancel out the few ממזר cases. That leaves an even doubt, and an even doubt is not a definite ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: An unmarried woman; her child is not a ממזר
Half and half; an even doubt

phrases.english: Since there is also the unmarried woman,
phrases.notes: She might abandon her baby out of shame, but her baby is not a ממזר.

phrases.english: and there are also those abandoned because of hunger,
it comes out half and half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's estimate of the odds that an אסופי is a ממזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אסופי is only a doubtful ממזר, with even odds.

steps.title: The Torah bans only a definite ממזר
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק "לא יבא ממזר בקהל ה׳" is read as banning only a definite ממזר from a congregation of definite lineage. A doubtful ממזר is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Torah said: "A ממזר shall not enter the congregation of ה׳." A definite ממזר may not enter, but a doubtful ממזר may enter. Into a congregation of definite lineage he may not enter, but into a congregation of doubtful lineage he may enter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings the פסוק that proves his ruling. The Torah only bans a ממזר we are sure about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ממזר is read as a sure ממזר, so a doubtful one is not included. The word קהל is read as a sure, clean congregation. Since an אסופי is only half and half, the Torah does not forbid him.

keyTerms.meaning: A child of a forbidden union, who may not marry into the community
The congregation, meaning Jews of fit lineage

steps.whatToRemember: By Torah law a doubtful ממזר like an אסופי is fit. Any ban on him comes from the Rabbis.

phrases.english: And the Torah said:
"A ממזר shall not enter the congregation of ה׳."
phrases.notes: דברים 23:3

phrases.english: It is a definite ממזר who may not enter,
but a doubtful ממזר may enter.
It is into a definite congregation that he may not enter,
but into a doubtful congregation he may enter.
phrases.notes: A "definite congregation" means people whose lineage is surely clean. A "doubtful" one means people whose lineage is unclear.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַתּוֹרָה אָמְרָה: לֹא יָבֹא מַמְזֵר בְּקָהָל ה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the Torah source showing that the half-and-half doubt makes the אסופי fit.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that by Torah law an אסופי is fit
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 23:3, read as banning only a definite ממזר from a definite congregation

steps.title: Why the Rabbis still call a foundling unfit
steps.stepSummary: The Rabbis made the אסופי unfit out of fear that he might marry his sister from his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they say a foundling is unfit? Lest he marry his sister from his father.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the Torah allows him, the גמרא explains why the Rabbis forbade the אסופי anyway. It gives the same reason it first gave for the שתוקי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the reason from step 22, now said about the אסופי. It sets up the same chain of questions that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Unfit, here meaning unfit to marry someone of clear lineage
His sister from his father; a half-sister through the father

phrases.english: And for what reason did they say a foundling is unfit?
Lest he marry his sister from his father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the rabbinic ban in spite of the Torah allowing him in step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban is a rabbinic decree, out of fear that he might marry his paternal sister.

steps.title: Then a foundling should not marry a female foundling
steps.stepSummary: If that is the fear, an אסופי should not marry an אסופית, since she might be his sister from either parent.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, a foundling should not marry a female foundling, lest he marry his sister from his father or from his mother!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. If we really fear he will marry his sister, two foundlings marrying each other is the biggest risk of all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אסופית's parents are both unknown, just like his. So she could be his sister from either parent, which is an even bigger risk. Yet two foundlings are allowed to marry, so the stated reason seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so; if you say that, then...

phrases.english: But if so,
a foundling should not marry a female foundling,
lest he marry his sister,
whether from his father or from his mother!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה אֲסוּפִי – אֲסוּפִית לֹא יִשָּׂא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the sister-fear reason given in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that the אסופי is unfit lest he marry his sister
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that fear is real, two foundlings, who could share either parent, should be forbidden to marry. They are not.

steps.title: Parents don't keep abandoning children
steps.stepSummary: It is unlikely that the same parents abandoned both a boy and a girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do all of these keep throwing away children?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that two foundlings are very unlikely to be siblings. Parents do not keep abandoning one child after another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each abandoned baby most likely comes from a different family. So the worry about a male and a female foundling being siblings is far-fetched.

phrases.english: Do all of these keep on throwing away children?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends against step 32 by calling the shared-parent case unlikely.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Probability: the feared case is unlikely
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two foundlings could easily be siblings.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is far-fetched that the same parents abandoned both.

steps.title: Then he couldn't even marry a foundling's daughter
steps.stepSummary: If we worry that much, an אסופי could not marry even the daughter of an אסופי, since her father might be his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he should not marry the daughter of a foundling, lest he marry his sister!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא hits back. If we worry about unlikely cases at all, we would have to forbid even more marriages, which we clearly do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A foundling's daughter has a known father, but that father has unknown roots. He could also have been the אסופי's father. Since nobody forbids this, worrying about rare cases cannot be the rule.

phrases.english: He should not marry the daughter of a foundling,
lest he marry his sister!
phrases.notes: Her father, the foundling, might secretly have fathered this young man too.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּת אֲסוּפִי לֹא יִשָּׂא, שֶׁמָּא יִשָּׂא אֲחוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that worrying about unlikely cases, which step 31's reason depends on, leads to an absurd result.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the Rabbis worry about rare sibling cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If rare cases count, he could not even marry a foundling's daughter, which is clearly allowed.

steps.title: The sister fear is too rare to explain the foundling ban
steps.stepSummary: The daughter of a foundling is permitted because a sister mix-up is rare. In the same way, the general sister fear is rare, so it cannot be why the רבנן made an אסופי פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is not common. So too, it is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that marrying a sister by accident is rare, so the decree 'lest he marry his sister' cannot explain why an אסופי is פסול. This sets up the real reason in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A foundling's daughter is allowed because a sister mix-up there is uncommon. By the same logic, the sister fear in general is uncommon, so the reason from step 31 falls away. This matches the result for the שתוקי in step 26.
steps.whatToRemember: An אסופי is fit by Torah law. The fear of a rare sister mix-up cannot explain the rabbinic ban, so the next step gives the real reason.

phrases.english: Rather, it is not common,
phrases.notes: This is the reason he may marry a foundling's daughter.

phrases.english: so too, it is not common.
phrases.notes: Meaning the general fear that he'll marry his sister is also rare, so it can't be the reason for the ban.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָא שְׁכִיחַ, הָכִי נָמֵי לָא שְׁכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 34 by applying the rule that rare cases are ignored.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because a sister mix-up is rare, the decree 'lest he marry his sister' cannot be the reason an אסופי is פסול, just as with the שתוקי.

steps.title: The Rabbis set a higher standard for families of clean lineage
steps.stepSummary: The real reason an אסופי may not marry someone of clean lineage is not a fear of marrying a relative. It is an extra protection the Rabbis made for families with clean lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the Rabbis made a higher standard for people with clean lineage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the 'he might marry his sister' reason and gives a new answer: this is simply an extra standard the Rabbis made to protect families with clean lineage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 34-35 the גמרא showed that the sister worry is too rare to matter. So the rule against an אסופי marrying a person of clean lineage needs a different reason. The new reason is a מעלה: a rabbinic 'raising of the bar' for מיוחסים, so they stay away from anyone whose background is unknown.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals that the earlier reason is dropped and a new one is given
A higher standard; an extra rabbinic stringency
People of clean, known family lineage

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on an אסופי marrying someone of clean lineage is a rabbinic מעלה (extra standard) for מיוחסים. It is not based on a fear that he might marry his sister.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the sister worry is still the reason. The גמרא has dropped it, so this rule only protects families of clean lineage. That is why the גמרא was willing to let an אסופי marry an אסופית.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why the restriction applies only toward families of clean lineage and not between two foundlings.

phrases.english: Rather, they made a higher standard regarding those of clean lineage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 35 showed the sister worry is too rare to matter, this step gives the real reason for the אסופי's restriction.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did the Rabbis forbid an אסופי from marrying someone of clean lineage?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a rabbinic higher standard (מעלה) made to protect families of clean lineage, not a fear of incest.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The restriction on an אסופי is a protective מעלה for מיוחסים.

steps.title: A new case: a foundling found already circumcised
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב הונא starts a new ruling about an abandoned child who was found already circumcised. His ruling comes in the next line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב הונא said: If one found him circumcised —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new statement. רבא בר רב הונא describes the case of a foundling found circumcised, and his ruling comes right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the discussion was about a regular אסופי and why he is restricted. Now a new אמורא brings a special detail: the baby was found already circumcised. That detail may change how we view the child, but the ruling itself only appears in the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who brings a new ruling about foundlings
One found him; the abandoned child was found

phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Huna said:
If one found him circumcised —
phrases.notes: "Him" is an abandoned baby. The sentence isn't finished yet; the ruling comes next.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא: מְצָאוֹ מָהוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The discussion of why an אסופי is restricted is finished, so this step opens a new topic about a special kind of foundling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opens the case of a foundling who was found circumcised. The ruling itself comes in the following text.
